chunks: And it has been narrated: "The Ka'bah complained to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, about what it suffered from the breaths of the polytheists.
So Allah, Exalted is He, revealed to it: 'Be at ease, O Ka'bah, for I shall replace them with a people who cleanse themselves with the branches of trees.'
Then when Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sent His Prophet Muḥammad صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, the Trustworthy Spirit, Jibrāʾīl عليه السلام, descended upon him with the siwak.

key_terms.الرُّوحُ الْأَمِينُ: the Trustworthy Spirit, meaning Jibrāʾīl عليه السلام
key_terms.الْكَعْبَةَ: the Ka'bah, the sacred House of Allah
key_terms.الْمُشْرِكِينَ: the polytheists whose breaths are mentioned as causing distress
key_terms.بِالسِّوَاكِ: with the siwak, the toothstick used for oral cleaning
key_terms.بِقُضْبَانِ الشَّجَرِ: with branches/twigs of trees, referring to toothsticks
key_terms.يَتَنَظَّفُونَ: they cleanse themselves; they practice cleanliness

ai.seo_question: What does the hadith say about the origin and significance of the siwak?
ai.summary: This hadith describes the Ka'bah's complaint about the impurity associated with the polytheists and Allah's promise to replace them with a people distinguished by cleanliness. It presents the siwak as part of the divinely brought sunnah conveyed to the Prophet Muḥammad صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم by Jibrāʾīl عليه السلام.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.125 - It has been narrated:
"The Kaaba complained to Allah (swt), Mighty and Majestic, about the distress it suffered from the breaths of the

polytheists.
Allah (swt), Exalted be He, revealed to it:
'Calm yourself, O’ Kaaba, for I will replace them with a people who purify themselves with branches of trees.'
When Allah (swt) sent His Prophet Muhammad (sw), the Trustworthy Spirit, Archangel Jibril (as), descended upon him with the siwak (toothstick)."
